constraints.name: Food Business Operator (FBO) status

citation.regulation: Regulation (EC) 852/2004 (retained UK law), Regulation (EC) 178/2002 (General Food Law)

constraints.rationale: If HarvestLink takes possession of food or relabels it as part of its logistics flow, rather than purely facilitating data-matching between producers and buyers, it crosses the line into becoming a Food Business Operator (FBO) itself — a status that carries registration and inspection duties under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 and the General Food Law that the platform is not currently structured to carry.
constraints.mitigation: Platform must operate strictly as a data/matching and documentation layer; producers and distributors remain the FBOs, never HarvestLink.
constraints.reasoning: Classified Red because the default/naive platform design (taking possession to simplify logistics) would trigger FBO status; the facilitation-only mitigation is a precedented pattern used by other UK marketplace/SaaS platforms to avoid a regulated-activity status they aren't built for, so requires_legal_review is not needed for this specific mitigation, though the boundary itself should still be legally confirmed (see open_items).

constraints.name: Traceability record integrity

citation.regulation: Regulation (EC) 178/2002, Article 18 (one step back, one step forward)

constraints.rationale: Traceability records generated on the platform will be relied on by foodservice buyers and enforcement bodies during a product recall to trace affected stock one step back and one step forward through the supply chain — integrity of those records has to be a deliberate design choice, not something assumed to fall out of the platform naturally.
constraints.mitigation: Require producer and distributor dual sign-off on every traceability record, with an immutable, append-only audit log.
constraints.reasoning: Amber because the requirement is well-defined by the regulation and the dual-sign-off/immutable-log mitigation is a standard technical pattern, not a novel legal question.

constraints.name: Allergen declaration liability

citation.regulation: Food Information (Amendment) (England) Regulations 2019 ("Natasha's Law"); Food Information Regulations 2014 / EU FIC Regulation 1169/2011

constraints.rationale: If HarvestLink were to auto-generate or edit an allergen declaration on a producer's behalf without that producer's explicit attestation, legal liability for an inaccurate declaration could shift from the producer (the actual FBO) onto HarvestLink itself, which is not a position the platform is built or licensed to hold.
constraints.mitigation: Allergen declarations must be producer-attested and signed off before finalising; HarvestLink is infrastructure, not the legal declarant.
constraints.reasoning: Amber because the liability-shifting risk is well understood and the producer-attestation mitigation is a standard, precedented pattern for platforms that facilitate but don't originate regulated content.

constraints.name: Data protection
constraints.rationale: Standard obligation for any platform handling producer and buyer business data — processing contact details, transaction records, and business information under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 is routine data-controller activity for a B2B marketplace, not a feasibility blocker on its own.
constraints.reasoning: Classified Green — this is an ongoing design/monitoring requirement common to virtually any B2B platform, not something specific or novel to HarvestLink's model.

overall_status.rationale: CON-01 (FBO status) is Red on its own, but it — along with both Amber items, CON-02 and CON-03 — has a concrete, precedented, non-legal-review mitigation already specified, so per the discount rule the overall verdict is one level better than the worst individual item, landing at Amber rather than Red.
